correctness.rationale: The normalized weighted harmonic monomials and all three exact angular compression cases were reconstructed. Direct coefficient multiplication gives one-band monomial commutators and their positive/negative tail coefficients equal to ∓(alpha+1)mn/k^2 with O(k^-3) remainder. For polynomial symbols, the leading Laurent symbol is f′ times conjugate g′ on the circle; the negative side is its reflection. The finite-Laurent counting lemma is proved by geometric block decomposition, finite-Toeplitz singular distribution via trace moments, and summable finite-rank boundary defects. The O(k^-3) band remainder has N(t)=O(t^-1/3), strictly negligible against t^-1/2. Counting inversion yields the coefficient 4(alpha+1)L^2 and exact p>1/2 threshold. The provided checker executed successfully with 411 assertions; none of the infinite conclusions depend on finite tests.

originality.rationale: The main full-text source proves qualitative vanishing rigidity of analytic/coanalytic harmonic Toeplitz commutators, not their exact singular distribution. The classical quasihomogeneous source proves symmetry and commutativity results for single Fourier modes; separately known monomial singular-value formulas are prior work, not the contribution. The new polynomial-pair coefficient depends on the modulus of the entire boundary derivative product and is not obtained by summing monomial singular values. The ambient-multiplication/projection commutator source concerns a distinct operator and an order-one rather than order-two singular law. No examined statement dominates the polynomial-pair Weyl coefficient, although a general pseudodifferential asymptotic theorem might indirectly imply it.
residual_risks: A more general microlocal or Birman–Solomyak singular-value Weyl theorem may subsume the weighted Laurent counting argument and thereby imply this specialization.
The closely related arXiv:2605.24698 full paper was not available; only its distinct abstract-level operator and singular order could be compared.
Historical publication priority and independent validation were not established.

value.rationale: The result determines the sharp weak-Schatten endpoint and an exact leading singular-value invariant for the natural all-polynomial class of analytic/coanalytic harmonic Bergman Toeplitz commutators. The boundary integral L is nonlinear in the coefficients and captures Fourier-diagonal interference absent from the previous single-monomial tables. It strengthens the new qualitative commutation theorem to a quantitative spectral law, with explicit weight dependence and a mathematically motivated trace-ideal threshold; it is not a routine scalar substitution.
